painPoints: Sprint 11 SCORE: 7.0/10. Strong engineering output (5 enhancements, 9/9/9 code quality, 7 new native tools) but ZERO persona retests. Improvement thesis unvalidated.

Sprint 11 DELIVERED: E1 execute-first routing (7 media intent patterns), E2 error handling (null guard + context-aware messages), E3 video intelligence (4 FFmpeg tools), E4 contact sheet + AI gateway, E5 cloud AI providers (Replicate + remove.bg).
Sprint 11 CRITICAL GAP: No retests performed. Marco 5.0 baseline never re-validated. hasAttachments always passed as false — undermines E1 routing. video-tools.ts registration unverified at runtime.
Sprint 11 TEST REGRESSION: 202 → 135 tests (-33%). New modules (video-tools, file-reference-detector, media-ai-gateway) have zero test coverage. Test-to-code ratio 1:10.3 (target 1:3-1:5).
Sprint 12 THEME: 'Validate & Wire — Proving the Media Pipeline Works'. Mandatory retests, test count restoration, runtime verification before new features.
Sprint 12 HARD GATES: (1) No sprint closes without persona retests. (2) Test count ≥ entry count. (3) Max 3 new enhancements. (4) hasAttachments fix is P0.
Sprint score trend: [8.0, 6.5, 7.0, 8.5, 7.5, 7.0, 6.6, 6.6, 5.87, 8.0, 7.0]. Stabilized after Sprint 10 recovery. Must validate to break through 8.0.
BRIGHT SPOTS: Research 8-9/10, Media AI gateway architecture extensible, 4-agent focus sprint more productive than 6-agent sprawl. Competitive moat: no rival platform offers 21+ media tools.

painPoints: Sprint 11 DELIVERED: Comprehensive AI technology assessment (28 sources). Two-tier stack recommendation: Tier 1 (local/free: sharp + fluent-ffmpeg + photo_engine.py), Tier 2 (cloud: Replicate Real-ESRGAN $0.0025/img + remove.bg $0.23/img). @tugrul/rembg (BiRefNet ONNX) as zero-cost local fallback.
Sprint 11 KEY FINDING: RMBG 2.0 achieves 90% accuracy — local background removal is now production-viable. No API key, no cost, instant results. This is a competitive moat.
Sprint 11 KEY FINDING: No competing AI agent platform (Manus, Devin, Cursor, Replit) offers media processing tools. Enso's 21+ media tools are UNIQUE in the market.
Sprint 11 DELIVERED: Cost analysis — Tier 1 Only $0/mo, Light (50 img/mo) $0-12/mo, Medium (200 img/mo) $0.50-47/mo. Projected Marco impact: 5.0 → 7.5-8.0 with recommended stack.

Sprint 12 ASSIGNMENT: (1) Research and prototype local RMBG 2.0 integration — evaluate @tugrul/rembg (BiRefNet ONNX) vs alternatives, validate Windows compatibility. (2) Research video AI APIs for Sprint 12+ video intelligence — scene detection, highlight extraction, auto-captioning.
Model cascading (60-70% cost reduction) still not adopted. Prompt caching for Claude/Gemini APIs still unimplemented. MCP integration patterns still unresearched.
No vision-based UI testing — persona retests use Puppeteer but agents cannot evaluate rendered screenshots programmatically.

personas.name: Marco Reyes
personas.background: Full-time visual storyteller — shoots commercial campaigns, weddings, travel content, and short-form video. His entire creative pipeline runs through his desktop: importing from camera cards, culling thousands of shots, batch editing in Lightroom/Capture One, color grading video in DaVinci Resolve, exporting for different platforms (Instagram reels, YouTube, client galleries, print). He discovered Enso's media and filesystem tools and now uses it as his creative command center — but more importantly, he sees AI as the biggest shift in visual media since digital replaced film. He's already using AI upscaling, generative fill, AI-powered color grading, and background removal in his daily work. He wants Enso to be the platform where cutting-edge AI image/video processing meets his professional workflow — not as toy demos, but as production-grade tools he relies on for paid client work.
goals: Use Enso as his media command center — browse shoot folders, view photos/videos, organize by project, cull selects vs rejects without opening Lightroom

Leverage AI for real production tasks — upscale low-res client photos, remove backgrounds for composites, generative fill to extend crops, AI color matching across a series, object removal from scenes

AI-powered video processing — auto-generate highlight reels from long footage, extract best frames, AI color grading to match reference looks, smart scene detection, auto-captioning for social media reels
Build custom AI-integrated tools for his workflow: AI-assisted culling (auto-detect sharpest shots, best expressions, duplicates), style transfer from reference images, batch AI enhancement pipelines
Manage his media archive — search across 500K+ files by date/camera/lens/location, find duplicates, track storage usage, identify unedited shoots

Stay on the cutting edge — use Enso's research and deep research to track latest AI image/video models (Flux, Stable Diffusion, Runway, Kling, Topaz), evaluate new tools, and build Enso apps that integrate the best ones into his pipeline
frustrations: Enso can browse files and show images but can't do real media operations — no batch rename, no format conversion, no EXIF reading, no contact sheet generation
The photo viewer is basic — needs side-by-side comparison, zoom, EXIF overlay, star ratings, flag/reject workflow like Lightroom's library module
No AI image processing built in — has to leave Enso to run upscaling (Topaz), background removal (remove.bg), or generative fill (Photoshop). These should be one-click operations inside Enso
No video intelligence at all — can't generate thumbnails, can't show duration/resolution/codec, can't extract stills from timecodes, no scene detection, no AI-powered highlight extraction

AI tools he's tried through Enso are surface-level demos — he needs production-grade quality (4x upscale without artifacts, clean background removal on hair/fur, color grading that matches a reference shot precisely)
No concept of a 'project' or 'shoot' in the media tools — everything is flat filesystem browsing, but his work is organized by shoot date + client + deliverable type
Cutting-edge AI models release monthly but he has no systematic way to evaluate them for his workflow — needs Enso to help him track, test, and integrate new models as they drop
